insights.headline: Gold holds $4,000 on central-bank buying as record yields shake out weak hands; Indian buyers adapt to ₹1.50 lakh gold.
insights.summary: Gold ended the week near $4,130–4,140 an ounce, its second straight weekly loss, as the 10-year US Treasury yield touched levels not seen since 2002. China's central bank added 20.2 tonnes in August, its largest monthly purchase since October 2023, and $18 billion of ETF inflows helped hold the $4,000 floor. In India, festive demand is adapting rather than fading: with 24-carat gold near ₹1.50 lakh per 10 grams, buyers are shifting to lightweight jewellery, old-gold exchanges and hallmarked pieces ahead of Diwali. MCX gold futures closed the week at ₹1,50,390/10g; silver at ₹2,25,877/kg.
points: Gold's $4,000 floor held on central-bank buying: China added 20.2 tonnes in August, its largest monthly purchase since October 2023.
Record US bond yields are the pressure point: the 10-year touched 5.34%, its highest since 2002, as traders priced ~80% odds of a Fed hold.
Indian festive buyers are adapting: lightweight jewellery, old-gold exchanges and hallmarked pieces as 24K gold sits near ₹1.50 lakh/10g.
India's silver imports rebounded to 15.5 mn ounces in August after licence bottlenecks choked May flows to ~1.5 mn ounces.
MCX silver options were manipulated via 1,238 unauthorised orders after a cyber breach; SEBI is reviewing position limits.

trending.title: The $4,000 floor holds — but the buyers have changed
trending.summary: Record 10-year yields (5.34%, highest since 2002) drove the weekly slide, yet China added 20.2 tonnes in August and gold funds drew $18bn. Kitco's survey shows Wall Street leaning bearish.

trending.title: Festive India isn't buying less gold — it's buying differently
trending.summary: With 24K gold near ₹1.50 lakh/10g, shoppers pick lightweight jewellery, exchange gold and demand hallmarks. The WGC sees festive and wedding demand improving, with digital gold picking up slack.

trending.title: Silver's India plumbing: licences cleared, options rigged
trending.summary: Silver imports rebounded to 15.5 mn oz in August from ~1.5 mn in May as licences cleared. A cyber breach enabled 1,238 unauthorised MCX silver options, spiking one from ₹174 to ₹2,300 in five minutes.

trending.title: Payrolls whipsaw, rupee bleeds
trending.summary: September payrolls (29,000 vs 90,000 expected) cooled Fed-hike bets before yields rebounded to 5.28%. The RBI sold dollars to steady the rupee as reserves fell $18.34bn — a third straight weekly drop.

items.title: Gold Tests $4,000 Floor as Record Bond Yields Collide With Central-Bank Buying
items.summary: Gold ended the week at $4,144.04 an ounce, down 3.4%, as the 10-year US Treasury yield touched 5.34% — its highest since 2002. Weak September payrolls (29,000 vs 90,000 expected) briefly cooled rate-hike bets, but selling resumed. Central-bank buying in China and Poland plus $18bn of August ETF inflows held the $4,000 floor. Bank of America keeps a $5,000 target, seeing $4,000 as the zone to hold.

items.title: Gold digs in above $4,000 as China's central bank adds 20.2 tons
items.summary: Gold ended Friday at $4,144.04 an ounce, holding above $4,000 despite a 3.4% weekly slide as US Treasury yields hit their highest since 2002. Reuters reports the floor is structural: China's central bank bought 20.2 tonnes in August — its largest monthly addition since October 2023 — extending its streak to 22 months and lifting reserves to 2,387 tonnes. Ghana's reserves also rose, to 25.2 tonnes.

items.title: Wall Street on the brink of bearish majority after gold's post-payrolls slide
items.summary: Kitco's weekly gold survey after Friday's slide shows Wall Street teetering on a bearish majority while Main Street abandoned the bullish bias it had held since July, after gold failed to hold above $4,200 and finished the week near session lows. Bannockburn's Marc Chandler likes gold higher next week on weak jobs and Fed patience; Adrian Day expects it lower; Adam Button stays neutral.

items.title: Comex Gold Ends the Week 3.59% Lower at $4133.70
items.summary: Comex gold for October delivery lost $154.10, or 3.59%, to $4,133.70 this week — the largest one-week decline since early June, the second straight weekly loss, and the lowest settlement since August 4. Silver fared worse, down 6.68% to $59.977, its lowest settlement since August 3. Year-to-date, gold is down 4.44% and silver 14.48%, per Dow Jones Market Data.

items.title: US yields rise, reversing initial reaction to weak jobs report
items.summary: US Treasury yields reversed an early decline after the weak September jobs report, the 10-year climbing 4.72 bps to 5.281% as traders priced ~80% odds of a Fed hold this month. Gold futures erased their payrolls pop — up 1.4% to $4,259, then down 1.2% to $4,153.80, the biggest blown gain in almost a month, per Dow Jones Market Data.

items.title: ₹1.50 lakh gold tests Indian consumers: Lightweight jewellery gains traction
items.summary: Gold's pullback from record highs may give Indian consumers a buying window ahead of Diwali and the wedding season. Buyers are shifting to lightweight jewellery to stay within budgets at the ₹1.50 lakh per 10-gram level, and Sky Gold & Diamonds' Mangesh Chauhan expects festive and wedding demand to hold steady.

items.title: Festive Gold Jewellery Demand Amid Elevated Prices: Changing Buying Trends
items.summary: Indian shoppers are adapting to elevated gold prices ahead of the festive season: choosing lighter-weight jewellery, exchanging old pieces, and insisting on hallmarked purchases rather than sitting out festive buying.

items.title: Gold Price in India Eases 7% Before Dhanteras: What Next
items.summary: Gold prices in India have eased about 7% ahead of Dhanteras, with the trade guarded and the World Gold Council describing sentiment as cautiously optimistic — wedding buying holding up, discretionary purchases softer. Digital gold is gaining: monthly purchases averaged about ₹25 billion in June–August, and Indian gold ETF assets stand near ₹1,912 billion.

items.title: Gold Demand Remains Strong Despite High Prices, Buyers Adjust Purchases
items.summary: The World Gold Council expects Indian gold demand to improve through the festive and wedding season on steady investment demand and resilient wedding buying despite near-record prices. With 24-carat gold around ₹1.48 lakh per 10 grams, Guwahati jewellers expect robust but smaller purchases — lighter jewellery, coins or digital gold — while old-gold exchange has widened domestic discounts.

items.title: Bullion Cues: Support fails
items.summary: MCX gold (December) futures ended the week at ₹1,50,390 per 10 grams, down 1.9%, while silver (December) closed at ₹2,25,877 per kg, down 3.8%, in The Hindu BusinessLine's weekly review. Gold held between ₹1,48,000 and ₹1,51,000 after Monday's gap-down, with a bearish bias below ₹1,52,000 and support at ₹1,44,000; silver's key support is ₹2,19,000.

items.title: Cyber manipulation in commodity market: Silver option price jumped from ₹174 to ₹2,300 in 5 minutes
items.summary: Cybercriminals breached a Noida risk-management firm's servers and used its static IP to place 1,238 unauthorized orders across 5,559 illiquid MCX silver option contracts. The contract spiked from ₹174 to ₹2,300 in five minutes; about ₹12 crore in premiums created false liquidity while counterparties siphoned roughly ₹11 crore. CERT-In confirmed deliberate distortion; one arrest made.

items.title: India's forex reserves fall $18.3 bn as RBI steps in to defend rupee
items.summary: India's forex reserves fell $18.34 billion in the week to September 25, the third straight weekly decline, RBI data showed. The kitty dropped to $747.56 billion from its September 4 record of $785.71 billion as the central bank sold dollars to steady the rupee; foreign currency assets fell $15.57 billion to $615.41 billion and gold reserves depleted $2.59 billion to $108.70 billion.

items.title: Silver demand in India didn't disappear; It was waiting for licences
items.summary: India's silver imports sank to about 1.5 million ounces in May after a duty rise and new licence rules, then rebounded to 15.5 million ounces in August once licences flowed, writes analyst Przemyslaw Radomski. Domestic prices now sit above import cost, keeping metal moving ahead of the festival season starting October 11 — though year-to-date imports are still about a quarter behind 2025.

items.title: SEBI examining position limits for non-agri contracts to boost liquidity
items.summary: SEBI chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said on Saturday the regulator is reviewing position limits for non-agricultural commodity derivatives — which include bullion contracts — to deepen liquidity and market depth without weakening risk controls. Consultations are complete and guidelines will follow; SEBI is also tackling GST frictions for exchange participants.

items.title: Tanvi Exports files for IPO: 5 key highlights from gold jewellery maker's DRHP
items.summary: Tanvi Exports India has filed a draft prospectus with SEBI for an IPO of up to 3.58 million shares plus an equal offer for sale, Mint reports. The Rajkot jewellery maker, 8% of Gujarat’s gold jewellery exports, will use the proceeds to repay debt and fund working capital. Revenue grew 188% CAGR to ₹11,399 million in FY2026; exports rose from ₹43.4 million to ₹2,457.5 million across five countries.

items.title: Gold Has Lost Its Luster but Here's How It Can Shine to Record Highs Again
items.summary: Goldman Sachs has reiterated its $4,900 year-end gold target despite September's Fed rate hike denting prices, arguing the metal should climb on strong central-bank reserve diversification as markets pare back expectations of further US hikes. Gold sat near $4,250 on Friday, well below its late-January peak above $5,600, pressured by rising yields even as soft jobs data cooled hike bets.
